Formatter functions

Source: R/format.R
fmt.Rd

Each fmt_*() function is the R form of a formatter class .x (rule 3.4.1). It returns a weft_text: a character vector whose attributes hold the printed record (rule 1.4.11), the number as printed, whether decimals are shown, and the relation ("=", "<" or ">"). Passing a weft_text to another formatter carries the record forward (rule 3.4.2).

Usage

fmt_num(x, digits = NULL, sigfig = NULL, unit = NULL, unit_form = NULL)

fmt_pct(x, digits = NULL, sigfig = NULL, unit = NULL)

fmt_sci(x, digits = NULL, sigfig = NULL, unit = NULL, unit_form = NULL)

fmt_no(x, unit_form = NULL)

fmt_word(x, unit_form = NULL)

fmt_count(x, unit_form = NULL)

fmt_ord(x, unit_form = NULL)

fmt_and(
  x,
  sep = ", ",
  last = NULL,
  trunc = NULL,
  none = NULL,
  unit_form = NULL
)

fmt_or(x, sep = ", ", last = NULL, trunc = NULL, none = NULL, unit_form = NULL)

fmt_p(x)

fmt_date(x)

fmt_range(x, digits = NULL, sigfig = NULL, unit = NULL, unit_form = NULL)

fmt_pairs(
  x,
  sep = ", ",
  last = NULL,
  trunc = NULL,
  none = NULL,
  unit_form = NULL
)

fmt_ul(x, none = NULL, unit_form = NULL)

fmt_ol(x, none = NULL, unit_form = NULL)

fmt_dl(x, none = NULL, unit_form = NULL)

fmt_cap(x)

fmt_a(x)

fmt_strong(x)

fmt_em(x)

Arguments

x

The value to format. A weft_text from another formatter is accepted.

digits

Decimal places. Not together with sigfig.

sigfig

Significant figures. Not together with digits.

unit

The unit to print a quantity in, as a string: fmt_num(u(150, "cm"), unit = "m") is "1.5 m". The quantity is converted first, so the number, the unit and the arm an n span chooses are all in that unit. A unit the quantity cannot be converted to, and unit on a value that is not a quantity, are a weft_value_error. Like digits, it implies .num. A ladder of units the author approves, written as one string with | between the units or as a character vector, unit = "mm|m|km" or unit = c("mm", "m", "km") (rule 4.4.23), prints in the first unit that gives a number from 1 up to, not including, 1,000, as the number is printed, and in one unit for a whole vector (the unit where most of its numbers fit, ties to the earlier). A number that fits no unit takes the one whose number is nearest the window, and zero the first. The order is the author's preference. Every unit on the ladder is checked, whichever is picked: one that does not convert, is refused or is the size of another is a weft_value_error, and an empty or repeated unit is a weft_construct_error. A ladder of one unit is that unit. The units attribute holds the unit picked. unit also converts a formatter's text that carries a quantity, as it converts the quantity itself. .sci with a ladder of more than one unit is a weft_value_error.

unit_form

How a quantity's unit prints (rule 3.4.8): NULL (the setting unit_form in force: "auto" unless _weft.yml or the document says otherwise, and for a weft_text input given a collapse class alone, each element's own printed form), "auto" (the symbol after digits, the name after a spelled number), "symbol", "name", or "none" (the number alone). Anything else is a weft_construct_error, and so is "symbol" on fmt_no(), fmt_word() and fmt_count(), and "name" when the document's lang is not English. A form other than "auto" on a value with no unit is a weft_value_error. fmt_pct() and fmt_p() take none.

sep

The text between items of a collapse.

last

The text before the final item of a collapse. The default is " and " (" or " for fmt_or()), with a comma before it when the serial_comma setting is on and there are three or more items; a last given here is used as it is.

trunc

The number of items a collapse shows before "and N others".

none

Text to print in place of a collapse when x is a vector of length zero (fmt_and(), fmt_or(), fmt_pairs(), fmt_ul(), fmt_ol(), fmt_dl()). The default, NULL, makes an empty vector a weft_no_value error. NULL itself is always an error.

Value

A weft_text.

Details

A missing value (NA, NaN, Inf, -Inf or a value of length zero) stops with an error of class weft_no_value. A value a class cannot take (a decimal given to fmt_word(), say) stops with class weft_value_error.

A number whose absolute value (for fmt_pct(), the percentage's) is below 1e-9 is zero and prints "0"; the quantity of a unit is not snapped, and a small one goes through the rule below as any other number does. Any other number prints to the default digits, however small: fmt_num(0.04) is "0.0" and fmt_pct(0.0004) is "0.0%", never "-0.0". When neither digits nor sigfig is given (a project default digits does not count) and fmt_num() or fmt_pct() prints a number that is not zero with no digit other than 0, the loss is not silent: a warned check of kind "printed as zero" is recorded as a failed claim(level = "warn") is (see claim()), and outside a knit it is a warning() of class weft_zero_warning. The value still prints. One warning is recorded for each call, however many elements print as zero; its message gives the first value, what printed and the count, and says to add sigfig to show the number or digits to confirm the zero. A bound of clamp() is never printed as zero: it prints as it was written.

A units value (see u()) prints with its unit, after a no-break space. The unit is its symbol or its name (rules 4.4.2, 4.4.15): the symbol after digits ("5 m"), the name after a spelled number or "no" ("five metres"), and unit_form can ask for either, or for none. The symbol text is Pandoc markdown: an exponent is a superscript (m^2^, and m to the minus three as m^-3^ with a true minus sign), a product is a middle dot, a unit with no numerator is written with negative powers, and characters markdown reads are escaped. A name is singular only when its number prints "1" or "one". A wording class that prints a word (fmt_word(), fmt_count(), fmt_no()) needs a name for the unit, judged on the class and never on the data: a unit with none is a weft_value_error (add it under units: in _weft.yml, or use unit_form = "none"). fmt_and(), fmt_or(), fmt_range() and glue_vec() print the unit once, after the last item, in that item's form; fmt_pairs(), fmt_ul(), fmt_ol(), fmt_dl() and a vector no collapse class joins print it with every element. fmt_pct(), fmt_p() and fmt_date() on a quantity that still has a unit are a weft_value_error; a ratio with no unit left is a plain number, and unit_form other than "auto" on it is a weft_value_error, as is fmt_ord() on a quantity with a unit (a rank has no unit). The result carries the attributes unit (the symbol text, for a plural number), unit_form ("symbol", "name" or NA for each element) and units (the unit as the units package gives it), so fmt_and(fmt_num(u(c(3, 5), m))) prints the unit once, and a number or wording class given the text formats its raw value afresh in the form then in force. The record's number and raw never hold the unit. # in a span or plural() prints what the governor prints as a value, unit included. See fmt_unit() for the unit alone.

Examples

fmt_num(3.14159)
#> <weft_text>
#> [1] "3.1"
fmt_pct(0.12)
#> <weft_text>
#> [1] "12%"
fmt_word(3)
#> <weft_text>
#> [1] "three"
fmt_and(c("a", "b", "c"))
#> <weft_text>
#> [1] "a, b and c"
